Competing scores either (a) provide only full-model AUROC with potentially non-comparable covariates (e.g., PGS000137 includes family history), (b) are pan-trait UKB sparse framework scores with modest PGS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS001321-001323), (c) report only effect sizes without PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS002761 OR=1.68), or (d) provide weaker/less-informative metrics (e.g., partial correlations in PGS001836/PGS002043) or smaller hit-based SNP sets. Limitation: the pool contains several strong, endpoint-faithful POAG/glaucoma candidates with incomplete or non-comparable performance reporting across studies (AUC often full-model only, covariate sets differ), so the apparent advantage of PGS001792 is not definitive and selection remains moderately uncertain.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant clinical subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), with phenotype alignment generally acceptable (many explicitly POAG; several generic glaucoma). The strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the context comes from the UK Biobank snpnet glaucoma set, where PGS001323 (Glaucoma time-to-event) reports the highest PGS-only metrics among listed models (PGS-only AUROC 0.61994; PGS R2 0.02201) and the largest incremental AUROC (0.0364) versus its close siblings PGS001321/PGS001322; these are explicitly PRS-only or incremental measures, unlike many other candidates that report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000137, PGS001792, PGS002741, PGS004944) which the provided domain guidance warns is not a valid substitute for PRS-only discrimination. Key limitation: PGS001323 uses a time-to-event (TTE) endpoint rather than a straightforward case-control glaucoma definition, and several other models are disease-focused POAG scores (e.g., PGS000137, PGS001792/PGS001797, PGS004944) but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 in the visible evidence, preventing a high-confidence selection.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) per trait/phenotyping fields. PGS004944 is best supported in the provided metadata by combining strong endpoint alignment (POAG), a very large validation sample (n=407,667), and a strong reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.74) alongside a reported AUROC (0.748). Competing models either report only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS000137 full-model AUROC=0.8 but includes family history as a covariate, making the AUROC likely covariate-inflated), come from pan-trait or portability frameworks with modest PRS-only metrics (e.g., UKB snpnet models), or provide weaker/less complete performance evidence. Main limitation: most candidates (including PGS004944) do not provide clearly PRS-only AUROC/R² in the visible fields, and AUROC values may be full-model and thus not directly comparable across different covariate sets; therefore the selection is supported but not definitive.

Direct-match candidates for glaucoma/primary open-angle glaucoma are present (15 total). PGS004944 is preferred because it is endpoint-aligned to the dominant clinical subtype (phenotyping_reported: primary open-angle glaucoma, self-reported) and provides comparatively strong PRS-comparable effect-size evidence (OR=1.74 with tight CI) alongside a reported AUROC (0.748) in a very large validation sample (n=407,667), with only basic covariates (age/age^2/sex/ancestry). However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and other plausible direct-match competitors exist with strong but differently reported metrics (e.g., PGS001792 full-model AUROC 0.777 with covariates-regressed-out R2=0.032; PGS000137 full-model AUROC 0.80 but includes family history covariate), making cross-model comparability imperfect from the visible metadata alone.

All listed candidates are direct matches to lupus erythematosus (either EFO: lupus erythematosus or systemic lupus erythematosus), but many have phenotype restrictions (e.g., early-onset only, renal/lupus nephritis subphenotypes, arthritis-outpatient context, or broad EHR ‘erythematous conditions’) and/or lack PRS-comparable metrics. PGS003960 has the cleanest endpoint alignment to the target as a generic systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis (phenotyping_reported: ‘Systemic lupus erythematosus’) and shows the strongest reported discrimination in the provided metadata (full-model AUROC 0.89 with CI 0.87–0.90) across a multi-ancestry evaluation set. However, this evidence is limited/confounded because the covariate explicitly includes a ‘phenotype risk score’ (a strong comparability/leakage warning per the domain guidance), and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental PRS contribution is shown; therefore the high AUROC cannot be interpreted as PRS-driven. Given this major limitation and the generally non-comparable full-model AUC reporting across candidates, the best available direct-match choice is still sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality.

Direct-match candidates for lupus erythematosus are present (notably PGS001870 and PGS002082 with trait_efo="lupus erythematosus"). Among these, PGS002082 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported "Lupus (localized and systemic)" matching the target umbrella concept) and a more modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (361,553) versus the much sparser penalized regression score PGS001870 (87 variants), which domain guidance suggests is structurally less reliable for polygenic traits when other evidence is similar. However, confidence is limited because neither lupus-erythematosus-labeled model reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 or effect-size metrics (only partial correlation), making performance comparisons and heritability sanity checks difficult; several SLE-only models report higher full-model AUROC but are not directly comparable and some use non-PRS covariate packaging (e.g., phenotype risk score), so overall the direct-match choice remains sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (including multiple systemic lupus erythematosus scores and two EFO-matched lupus erythematosus umbrella scores). PGS000328 is preferred because it targets systemic lupus erythematosus with a direct-onset-related phenotype and reports strong discrimination in European validation (full-model AUROC=0.83; n=1,001), outperforming other SLE candidates that report lower AUROC (e.g., 0.79, 0.65, 0.576) and avoiding explicit phenotype-derived clinical packaging. Main limitation: across the candidate set, reported metrics are largely full-model (no clear PGS-only AUROC/R2), covariates are often unknown, and the top-AUROC SLE candidate (PGS003960, AUROC=0.89) is explicitly adjusted for a phenotype risk score (non-genetic packaging/leakage), reducing comparability and keeping overall confidence below high.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus, including exact EFO matches (PGS001870, PGS002082) and closely aligned systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) models. PGS002082 is the best-supported direct match because it targets the exact query EFO term (lupus erythematosus) with endpoint-aligned phenotyping ('Lupus (localized and systemic)') and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (361,553), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits over sparse UKB portability alternatives and GWAS-hit-only scores. However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because no PRS-only AUROC/R² is reported for PGS002082 (only partial correlation), and several SLE-focused models report higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS003960 AUROC 0.89) but are penalized by non-comparable covariate packaging (phenotype risk score) and/or subtype-restricted endpoints; thus, the visible metadata does not provide a clean, directly comparable performance basis to upgrade confidence to high.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (both systemic lupus erythematosus and broader lupus erythematosus EFO). PGS000328 is selected because it has a direct SLE endpoint (trait_reported/systemic lupus erythematosus) with a relatively strong reported discrimination signal among the pool (full-model AUROC=0.83 in European validation, n=1,001), and it is disease-focused rather than a UK Biobank portability framework score. Main limitation: across candidates, reported metrics are largely full-model (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are absent), covariates are often unknown, and some alternatives have non-comparable or potentially inflated packaging (e.g., PGS003960 uses a phenotype risk score covariate) or endpoint restrictions (renal/nephritis/early-onset). These issues make the evidence insufficient to call a single clearly high-quality standalone PRS winner with high confidence.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (multiple systemic lupus erythematosus models plus two EFO-level lupus erythematosus models). PGS000328 is preferred because it targets systemic lupus erythematosus with a clear disease-aligned endpoint (reported as SLE with early onset) and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the straightforward disease PRS candidates (full-model AUROC 0.83 in European validation, n=1,001), exceeding other SLE candidates with reported AUROC (e.g., 0.79 for PGS000196; 0.65 for PGS000754; ~0.58 for PGS000771). Main limitation: across the set, the available performance is largely full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and generally lacks PRS-only metrics; additionally, PGS003960 reports a higher AUROC (0.89) but is confounded by explicit phenotype-risk-score covariate packaging (non-comparable leakage per provided domain knowledge), and the UKB portability lupus-erythematosus-labeled models (PGS001870/PGS002082) provide only weak partial-correlation metrics, leaving residual uncertainty about true standalone PRS performance. Hence the direct match is real but the evidence is insufficient for a high-confidence, clearly best choice.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (both systemic lupus erythematosus and broader lupus endpoints). PGS000328 is preferred because it targets systemic lupus erythematosus with a clear lupus diagnosis phenotype (early-onset SLE), has straightforward GWAS-hit construction (57 variants), and reports comparatively strong discrimination in its selected European validation (full-model AUROC=0.83; n=1,001), which is higher than other non-packaged SLE candidates shown (e.g., PGS000196 AUROC=0.79; PGS000754 AUROC=0.65; PGS000771 AUROC=0.576). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with unknown covariates (no PGS-only AUC/R2 available), and some other high-AUROC models are potentially non-comparable due to explicit clinical packaging (e.g., PGS003960 uses a phenotype risk score covariate), making it hard to cleanly rank PRS signal across the entire set.

All 12 candidates are direct matches to lupus erythematosus/SLE at the concept level, but several have endpoint restrictions or non-comparable covariate packaging that limit clear selection. PGS002082 is preferred because it targets the exact catalog trait (“Lupus (localized and systemic)” with trait_efo=lupus erythematosus and matching phenotyping_reported), is derived with a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (361,553), and is evaluated across multiple ancestry groups (including EUR) in a portability setting, providing some evidence of transfer context beyond a single homogeneous cohort. Key limitation: its reported performance is only a modest partial correlation (partial-r=0.0212) rather than PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, and many competing SLE-specific models report higher full-model AUROCs; however, those AUROCs are not PRS-only and in one case are explicitly confounded by phenotype-risk-score covariates (PGS003960), while others have more phenotype restrictions (e.g., early-onset, renal manifestations). Therefore a direct match exists, but the available, comparable evidence is insufficient to label any option as clearly high-quality.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (both generic lupus erythematosus and systemic lupus erythematosus). For the target trait "lupus erythematosus" (EFO: lupus erythematosus), the cleanest concept-aligned models are PGS001870 and PGS002082 (both "Lupus (localized and systemic)"; phenotyping_reported matches; UKB portability framework). Between these two, PGS002082 is preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 361,553 variants vs penalized regression with 87 variants) and has slightly stronger reported partial correlation (0.0212 vs 0.0184) in the selected European validation record. Main limitation: neither score reports PRS-only AUROC or PRS-only R2, and many other candidates report higher full-model AUROC but are not directly comparable because they are SLE-specific and/or use non-PRS covariates (e.g., phenotype risk score in PGS003960) or restricted/sub-phenotypes; therefore the recommendation remains sub-optimal with only moderate confidence.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus, including multiple systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) PRS and two umbrella-phenotype models explicitly mapped to EFO "lupus erythematosus". PGS000328 is preferred because it targets SLE with a clear lupus diagnosis endpoint (early-onset SLE), reports the strongest discrimination among the SLE candidates that do not have obvious non-genetic phenotype/clinical-risk packaging (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR; n=1,001), and is disease-focused rather than a portability-framework score. Key limitation: across the candidate set, performance reporting is largely full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), covariates are mostly unknown, and at least one high-AUROC option (PGS003960) is explicitly adjusted for a phenotype risk score (non-genetic packaging), making cross-model metric comparability weak; additionally, PGS000328’s endpoint is restricted (onset before age 20) rather than generic lupus erythematosus, so the direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). Among these, PGS000788 has the strongest visible validation discrimination metrics in Europeans (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) and a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.53–1.88), with endpoint fidelity aligned to the target via an incident lymphocytic leukemia phenotype. However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), limiting cross-model comparability per the provided domain guidance; additionally, PGS000788’s construction is described as an inverse-weight variant of PGS000077, creating ambiguity about why it should be intrinsically better as a standalone PRS. Competing direct matches (e.g., PGS000077 with HR 1.45 and AUROC 0.719; PGS000645 with much lower AUROC 0.578 and only 6 variants; PGS002305 with AUROC 0.57 on small n=265) appear weaker on the visible metrics, but the lack of PRS-only metrics across the pool prevents a high-confidence, high-quality direct selection.

All 13 candidates are direct-match for the target trait concept (lymphoid/lymphocytic/chronic lymphocytic leukemia all map within the provided context to lymphoid leukemia EFO, with phenotyping largely being direct diagnosis endpoints). Among the broad lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia (not CLL-only) models, PGS000788 shows the strongest visible validation performance evidence (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756; HR per SD 1.7 with CI 1.53–1.88) on an incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and large European evaluation (n=391,338). However, selection remains sub-optimal because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC / PRS-only R² or incremental AUROC) are not reported for any of the leading broad-endpoint candidates, and the PGS000788 method description indicates it is a re-weighted derivative of PGS000077 rather than an independently derived score—so the apparent edge is based on full-model metrics/effect size rather than clearly isolated PRS performance.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), and several close-subtype candidates (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) are also present but are not exact matches to the target trait. Among the direct matches, PGS000788 has the strongest visible discrimination evidence in European evaluation (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756; HR per SD 1.7 [1.53–1.88]) with phenotype-aligned endpoint ('Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia') and only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, all candidates primarily report full-model metrics rather than clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², so cross-model performance comparability is limited; additionally, PGS000788 is described as using inverse weights derived from PGS000077, creating some ambiguity about the underlying PRS construction and whether its apparent advantage reflects PRS differences versus modeling choices. These limitations prevent a high-confidence, high-quality designation despite PGS000788 being the best-supported direct-match option in the provided context.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (lymphoid leukemia / lymphocytic leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). Among these, PGS000788 has the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence in European evaluation with AUROC=0.738, C-index=0.756, and HR per SD=1.70 (strong signal), with phenotype alignment to incident lymphocytic leukemia and only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, selection remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 shown), and PGS000788’s construction is described as using inverse variant weights from PGS000077, creating ambiguity about whether it is a robust, principled PRS versus a framework/packaging variant; additionally, other direct-match options (e.g., PGS000077 with similar endpoint and large evaluation) are close but lack comparable PRS-only metrics as well.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait (lymphoid leukemia), including broad lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia scores (PGS000077, PGS000788, PGS000645) and subtype-focused chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) scores (e.g., PGS000646/647/648/649/650/651, PGS000874, PGS003453). PGS000874 is the best-supported single choice in the visible evidence because it targets the clinically close diagnosis of CLL with a clear disease endpoint, reports strong discrimination/effect evidence (C-index 0.861; OR 3.79), and has a multi-ancestry evaluation (including EUR), whereas the broad lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia options mainly provide full-model AUROC/HR without PRS-only metrics and appear to come from cross-cancer/pan-cancer frameworks where full-model AUROC may be covariate-driven. Main limitation: PGS000874’s phenotyping is explicitly restricted to individuals with a family history of hematological cancers, which reduces generalizability to generic lymphoid leukemia risk and makes the direct-match recommendation sub-optimal despite strong reported metrics.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid (lymphocytic) leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), plus several chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) subtype models. Among the direct lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia models, PGS000788 has the strongest visible discriminative signal in effect size (HR per SD 1.7, 95% CI 1.53–1.88) and slightly higher full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) compared with PGS000077 (HR 1.45; AUROC 0.719) and markedly better than the smaller PRSweb lymphoid leukemia model PGS000645 (AUROC 0.578; OR per SD 1.358). Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for the target trait (phenotyping_reported: incident lymphocytic leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia) with only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Main limitation: none of these candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R² (the AUROC shown is full-model), so cross-model ranking relies heavily on effect size and endpoint coherence; additionally, PGS000788’s method description notes it reuses the 75 variants from PGS000077 with inverse weights, creating ambiguity about why it appears stronger based on metadata alone, so the recommendation cannot be high-confidence.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid (lymphocytic) leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), and several chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) subtype models are also present but are less directly aligned to the broader target trait. Among the direct lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia candidates, PGS000788 has the strongest visible discrimination/effect-size evidence in a large European evaluation (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756; HR 1.7 per SD) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and its endpoint (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”) aligns well with the target disease concept. However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), and PGS000788’s method description indicates it is derived from PGS000077 with inverse weights, creating ambiguity about the true standalone PRS quality and comparability across candidates.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305), with several additional subtype models for chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Among the direct lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia models, PGS000788 shows the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence in European evaluation (full-model AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756; HR per SD 1.7 with CI 1.53–1.88) and has endpoint alignment via phenotyping_reported = incident lymphocytic leukemia. However, selection is limited by comparability concerns: available AUC/C-index are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), and PGS000788’s method description indicates it is a re-weighted variant of PGS000077 (“inverse variant weights”), creating uncertainty about PRS construction/interpretability relative to a straightforward GWAS-significant variant score. Given multiple plausible direct-match alternatives with weaker but more conventional setups (e.g., PGS000077 HR 1.45; PGS000645 OR 1.36; PGS002305 AUROC 0.57) and the lack of PRS-only metrics across the set, the best choice is not unequivocally clear, so confidence is moderate and the outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (lymphoid/lymphocytic leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). PGS000077 is preferred because it has coherent phenotype alignment (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; phenotyping_reported=Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) and reports supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.45 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.61) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and large European validation (n=391,338). The main limitation is that the available discrimination metric is a full-model AUROC/C-index (AUROC 0.719; C-index 0.735) rather than PRS-only performance, and another direct-match candidate (PGS000788) shows higher full-model metrics (AUROC 0.738; HR 1.7) but is described as an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000077 with an unusually high reported R² (0.415) that is not clearly PRS-only and is difficult to interpret under the provided heritability sanity-check guidance. Given these metric-comparability uncertainties across candidates, the selection is direct-match but not high-confidence.

Direct-match candidates are present for lymphoid leukemia, but the pool mixes broader lymphoid-leukemia endpoints (e.g., incident lymphocytic leukemia) with subtype-specific chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) scores, making it unclear that any single model is optimal for the broad target without a subtype decision. PGS000874 is best supported on visible PRS signal strength and validation evidence: it is a CLL-focused score with strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.861, OR 3.79) and multi-ancestry evaluation (NR/AFR/EUR/MAE). However, it has a notable endpoint restriction (CLL in individuals with a family history of hematological cancers), which may limit generalizability to unselected ‘lymphoid leukemia’ and prevents a high-confidence direct-match designation. Competing broader-label models (PGS000077/PGS000788) have large European validation and moderate HRs (1.45–1.7) but report only full-model metrics (AUROC/C-index) and are from cross-cancer/pan-cancer contexts, making PRS-only comparability and ranking against the CLL-focused evidence unresolved.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with key differences in endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS001274 is preferred because it provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.57595; PGS R2 0.00945) plus incremental AUROC (0.00777) under basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and uses a closely aligned clinical endpoint (osteoporosis without pathological fracture) rather than a proxy trait. Competing models largely lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (many report only OR/beta or incremental R2), making them harder to rank; PGS001273 is the closest alternative with similar metadata but slightly weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5685; PGS R2 0.00688). The main limitation is that the chosen model’s endpoint is a subtype/time-to-event definition rather than the broad generic osteoporosis diagnosis, which lowers confidence despite strong comparability of the reported PRS-only metrics.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (trait_efo includes osteoporosis and phenotyping_reported is osteoporosis or closely aligned ICD10 M81/M80 variants). Among them, PGS001274 provides the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.57595) and PGS-only R2 (0.00945) plus incremental AUROC (0.00777) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making its discrimination evidence more directly attributable to the PRS than models that report only full-model metrics or only effect sizes/partial correlations. The main limitation is that its endpoint is time-to-event osteoporosis without pathological fracture rather than a generic case-control osteoporosis definition, and several newer candidates (e.g., PGS004565/PGS004560) use multi-score aggregation methods with higher per-SD ORs but lack comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2 and have unknown covariates, preventing a high-confidence best-in-class choice from the visible metadata alone.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis by trait fields. Several (e.g., PGS001273/PGS001274) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework; despite reporting PRS-only AUROC/R2, their very high full-model AUROC with only small incremental AUROC and small PGS-only R2 suggests covariate-driven discrimination and framework-origin scores are generally weaker external choices per the provided domain guidance. Many newer UKB-derived models (PGS004490/PGS004495/PGS004560/PGS004565) have unknown covariates and report only modest per-SD ORs, and the portability-study models (PGS001883/PGS002095) provide only partial-correlation metrics without clearer PRS-comparable discrimination. PGS002768 aligns cleanly to the generic osteoporosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), evaluates in EUR, and provides a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38), which is usable PRS-quality evidence when AUROC/R2 are missing. Limitation: across the pool, many candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS002768 itself does not report PRS-only metrics, so the selection is based on endpoint fidelity + method family + effect-size evidence rather than head-to-head comparable discrimination.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis by trait_reported/trait_efo and (for most) phenotyping_reported. Among models with PRS-comparable metrics explicitly reported, the snpnet UKB models (PGS001273/PGS001274) provide the clearest PRS-only evidence (PGS AUROC no covariates and PGS R2 no covariates) plus incremental AUROC, enabling a more comparable assessment than candidates reporting only OR/beta or partial-r. Between the two, PGS001274 has slightly stronger PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.57595 vs 0.5685; PGS-only R2 0.00945 vs 0.00688) and higher incremental AUROC (0.00777 vs 0.00477) with similar covariates and validation ancestry, supporting it as the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. Limitation: its endpoint is time-to-event ‘osteoporosis without pathological fracture’, which is somewhat narrower than generic osteoporosis, and the strongest-looking effect-size models (e.g., metaPRS OR~1.33; PRS-CS OR 1.31) lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and/or have unknown covariates, preventing a high-confidence selection.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) based on trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS002768 provides the strongest PRS-comparable signal in the visible evidence: an explicit per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) in a European evaluation sample (n=39,444) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates), which is informative even without AUROC/R2. Competing candidates either (a) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (PGS001273/PGS001274) where the very high full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven given small incremental AUROC and low PGS-only R2, and/or (b) lack comparable PRS-only metrics and show weaker/less interpretable evidence (e.g., partial correlations for PGS001883/PGS002095; unknown covariates and modest ORs for PGS004495/PGS004565; beta-only reporting for EAS-focused PGS005146/PGS005155). Main limitation: several models lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2, and the pool mixes endpoints (e.g., M81, time-to-event), so the preference for PGS002768 is driven primarily by endpoint alignment plus the clearest effect-size evidence rather than a head-to-head PRS-only discrimination comparison.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but most lack PRS-comparable metrics (AUC/R2) and several are from pan-trait/portability frameworks or have unknown covariates. The snpnet UKB framework scores (PGS001273/PGS001274) report PGS-only AUROC (~0.57) and PGS-only R2 (~0.007–0.009), but their very high full-model AUROC (~0.79) is largely covariate-driven given the small incremental AUROC, consistent with the domain guidance not to substitute full-model AUROC for PRS performance. Among the candidates with effect-size evidence, PGS002768 (PRS-CS; EUR GWAS and EUR evaluation; phenotyping_reported Osteoporosis) reports OR=1.31 (1.25–1.38) per SD, which is a moderately supportive PRS-quality signal and is more directly comparable than models that provide only uncontextualized beta or lower ORs (e.g., OR~1.18–1.33 with unknown covariates in the 2024 Commun Biol family). Main limitation: many candidates have incomplete/heterogeneous reporting and there is no clear head-to-head comparison on the same metric across the top contenders, so the preference for PGS002768 is based on endpoint fidelity plus the strongest clean, interpretable effect-size evidence available in this context rather than definitive superior discrimination.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis at the concept level (trait_efo includes osteoporosis; phenotyping_reported is osteoporosis or closely related ICD10 subtype M81). However, confidence is limited because key performance comparability is mixed across candidates: the snpnet UKB pan-trait models (PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334) uniquely report explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 but are from a known sparse pan-trait framework and show small PRS-only metrics; meanwhile the newer J44 models (PGS004466/PGS004536) report only per-SD ORs with unknown covariates and lack PRS-only AUC/R2.
